RADS (Regionale Akutte Diagnostik og BehandlingsStandarder) is a set of clinical guidelines focused on regional acute diagnostics and treatment standards [^src1]. Within the framework of the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK), increasing adherence to RADS is a key objective for improving the quality of patient care [^src1]. Specifically, compliance with RADS and the guidelines from the Danish Society of Cardiology (Dansk Cardiologisk Selskab) directly influences the quality of treatment measured by Indicator 15 [^src1]. Indicator 15 is a healthcare quality metric that tracks the incidence of heart failure within one year after a patient receives a new diagnosis of atrial fibrillation [^src1]. 

The current corpus provides limited information on RADS, mentioning it solely in the context of AFDK's quality development goals and Indicator 15. No further details regarding the specific clinical protocols, authorship, or publication history of the RADS guidelines are available in the provided documents.
